title: 量词否定：¬∀x(P→Q) 的正确与错误写法
expected_output:
x    : 0 1 2 3 4
P(x) : 1 1 0 1 0
Q(x) : 1 0 0 1 1

LHS  ~(forall x (P(x)->Q(x)))      = 1
RHS1 exists x (P(x) ^ ~Q(x))       = 1   <- correct negation
RHS2 exists x (P(x) -> ~Q(x))      = 1   <- wrong (too weak)

LHS == RHS1 ? yes
LHS == RHS2 ? yes

counterexample witness for RHS1: x=1 (P=1, Q=0)
why RHS2 is wrong: it is also true at an x with P(x)=0,
so it can hold even when the universal statement is still true.
